from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import sqlite3
import threading
from contextlib import contextmanager
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable, Iterator

from .model import epoch_millis

# One truncation event, as handed to :meth:`Store.insert_truncation`.
TruncationRecord = tuple[str, str, str, int, int, int]

ACTION_VERSION_APPENDED = "version_appended"
ACTION_WINDOW_TRUNCATED = "window_truncated"


class Store:
    """Append-only persistence for entity versions.

    Rows in ``versions`` are never deleted.  A correction appends its own row
    and closes the ``valid_end`` of the value it supersedes; every closing is
    also appended to ``truncations``, which records *when the system learned*
    the bound, so a transaction-time reader can tell a declared bound from one a
    later correction pulled back.
    """

    def __init__(self, path: str, clock: Callable[[], datetime] | None = None):
        if path != ":memory:":
            Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.clock = clock or (lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc))
        # One connection is shared across request threads, so every use of it is
        # serialised by this lock.  A write holds it across its whole
        # transaction, which is what commits different batches one after another
        # (continuous versions, non-overlapping windows) and stops any reader on
        # another thread observing a half-applied batch.  It is reentrant so the
        # read helpers a write calls while holding the lock can take it again.
        self.lock = threading.RLock()
        self.connection = sqlite3.connect(path, isolation_level=None, check_same_thread=False)
        self.connection.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        self.connection.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL")
        self.connection.executescript(
            """
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS entities (
              type TEXT NOT NULL,
              id TEXT NOT NULL,
              created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
              PRIMARY KEY (type, id)
            );
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS versions (
              type TEXT NOT NULL,
              id TEXT NOT NULL,
              attribute TEXT NOT NULL,
              version INTEGER NOT NULL,
              operation TEXT NOT NULL,
              value TEXT,
              valid_from INTEGER NOT NULL,
              valid_end INTEGER,
              declared_end INTEGER,
              recorded_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
              PRIMARY KEY (type, id, attribute, version)
            );
            CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS versions_by_attribute
              ON versions(type, id, attribute, valid_from);
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS truncations (
              type TEXT NOT NULL,
              id TEXT NOT NULL,
              attribute TEXT NOT NULL,
              version INTEGER NOT NULL,
              recorded_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
              valid_end INTEGER NOT NULL
            );
            CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS truncations_by_version
              ON truncations(type, id, attribute, version, recorded_at);
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS idempotency (
              key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
              operation TEXT NOT NULL,
              response TEXT NOT NULL
            );
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS audit_events (
              seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
              event_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
              recorded_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
              action TEXT NOT NULL,
              type TEXT NOT NULL,
              id TEXT NOT NULL,
              attribute TEXT NOT NULL,
              version INTEGER NOT NULL,
              operation TEXT,
              value TEXT,
              valid_from INTEGER,
              declared_end INTEGER,
              valid_end INTEGER
            );
            CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS audit_events_scan
              ON audit_events(recorded_at, event_id);
            """
        )
        self._backfill_audit()

    @staticmethod
    def audit_event_id(*parts: Any) -> str:
        """Deterministic, collision-resistant identity for one audit item.

        The digest is taken over the immutable ledger coordinates of the event
        — its action, entity coordinates, version, transaction instant, and the
        payload the write committed — so the same committed row always derives
        the same id, while two distinct events cannot share one.  A version
        later corrected carries different coordinates and therefore a different
        id, so an old audit item can never be retroactively rewritten.
        """
        joined = "\x1f".join("" if part is None else str(part) for part in parts)
        return hashlib.sha256(joined.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

    def _backfill_audit(self) -> None:
        """Project rows written by older releases into the audit ledger.

        Databases created before the audit entry point existed hold committed
        ``versions`` and ``truncations`` rows but no audit items.  Every such
        row is described once here, in the same deterministic order fresh
        writes use: transaction time first, then stable entity and version
        coordinates.

        Each projection runs in one transaction, so a crash can never leave it
        half applied; the UNIQUE index on ``event_id`` makes a re-run idempotent
        as well, so reopening a database can never double-fill it.
        """
        with self.lock:
            already = self.connection.execute(
                "SELECT 1 FROM audit_events WHERE action = ? LIMIT 1",
                (ACTION_VERSION_APPENDED,),
            ).fetchone()
            if already is None:
                version_rows = self.connection.execute(
                    """
                    SELECT type, id, attribute, version, operation, value,
                           valid_from, declared_end, recorded_at
                      FROM versions
                     ORDER BY recorded_at, type, id, attribute, version
                    """
                ).fetchall()
                legacy: list[tuple[Any, ...]] = []
                for row in version_rows:
                    event_id = self.audit_event_id(
                        ACTION_VERSION_APPENDED,
                        row["type"], row["id"], row["attribute"], row["version"],
                        row["recorded_at"], row["operation"], row["value"],
                        row["valid_from"], row["declared_end"],
                    )
                    legacy.append(
                        (
                            event_id,
                            int(row["recorded_at"]),
                            ACTION_VERSION_APPENDED,
                            row["type"], row["id"], row["attribute"], int(row["version"]),
                            row["operation"], row["value"],
                            int(row["valid_from"]), row["declared_end"], None,
                        )
                    )
                if legacy:
                    self.connection.execute("BEGIN")
                    try:
                        self.connection.executemany(
                            """
                            INSERT OR IGNORE INTO audit_events(
                                event_id, recorded_at, action, type, id, attribute, version,
                                operation, value, valid_from, declared_end, valid_end)
                            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
                            """,
                            legacy,
                        )
                    except Exception:
                        self.connection.execute("ROLLBACK")
                        raise
                    else:
                        self.connection.execute("COMMIT")
            already = self.connection.execute(
                "SELECT 1 FROM audit_events WHERE action = ? LIMIT 1",
                (ACTION_WINDOW_TRUNCATED,),
            ).fetchone()
            if already is None:
                truncation_rows = self.connection.execute(
                    """
                    SELECT rowid, type, id, attribute, version, recorded_at, valid_end
                      FROM truncations
                     ORDER BY recorded_at, type, id, attribute, version, valid_end, rowid
                    """
                ).fetchall()
                legacy = []
                for row in truncation_rows:
                    event_id = self.audit_event_id(
                        ACTION_WINDOW_TRUNCATED,
                        row["type"], row["id"], row["attribute"], row["version"],
                        row["recorded_at"], row["valid_end"], row["rowid"],
                    )
                    legacy.append(
                        (
                            event_id,
                            int(row["recorded_at"]),
                            ACTION_WINDOW_TRUNCATED,
                            row["type"], row["id"], row["attribute"], int(row["version"]),
                            None, None, None, None, int(row["valid_end"]),
                        )
                    )
                if legacy:
                    self.connection.execute("BEGIN")
                    try:
                        self.connection.executemany(
                            """
                            INSERT OR IGNORE INTO audit_events(
                                event_id, recorded_at, action, type, id, attribute, version,
                                operation, value, valid_from, declared_end, valid_end)
                            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
                            """,
                            legacy,
                        )
                    except Exception:
                        self.connection.execute("ROLLBACK")
                        raise
                    else:
                        self.connection.execute("COMMIT")

    @contextmanager
    def transaction(self) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
        # Serialise whole transactions: BEGIN IMMEDIATE takes the write lock at
        # once, and the RLock keeps every other thread (readers included) off the
        # shared connection until COMMIT, so a batch is atomic to the outside.
        with self.lock:
            self.connection.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
            try:
                yield self.connection
            except Exception:
                self.connection.execute("ROLLBACK")
                raise
            else:
                self.connection.execute("COMMIT")

    def now(self) -> int:
        """Current instant as integer milliseconds since the Unix epoch."""
        return epoch_millis(self.clock().astimezone(timezone.utc))

    @staticmethod
    def encode(value: Any) -> str:
        return json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True)

    @staticmethod
    def decode(value: str) -> Any:
        return json.loads(value)

    # -- entity bookkeeping -------------------------------------------------

    def entity_row(self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:
        with self.lock:
            return self.connection.execute(
                "SELECT created_at FROM entities WHERE type = ? AND id = ?",
                (entity_type, entity_id),
            ).fetchone()

    def insert_entity(self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str, created_at: int) -> None:
        self.connection.execute(
            "INSERT INTO entities(type, id, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
            (entity_type, entity_id, created_at),
        )

    def entity_keys(
        self, entity_type: str | None = None, entity_id: str | None = None
    ) -> list[tuple[str, str, int]]:
        """Every entity in scope, with its record instant, in stable order.

        A ``type`` alone selects every entity of that type, a ``type``/``id``
        pair one entity, and no argument the whole store.  Rows come back
        ordered by the stable identifier ``(type, id)``, so a caller walking
        the result always visits entities in the same sequence.
        """
        clauses = []
        parameters = []
        if entity_type is not None:
            clauses.append("type = ?")
            parameters.append(entity_type)
        if entity_id is not None:
            clauses.append("id = ?")
            parameters.append(entity_id)
        where = "" if not clauses else " WHERE " + " AND ".join(clauses)
        with self.lock:
            rows = self.connection.execute(
                f"SELECT type, id, created_at FROM entities{where} ORDER BY type, id",
                parameters,
            ).fetchall()
        return [(str(row["type"]), str(row["id"]), int(row["created_at"])) for row in rows]

    # -- versions -----------------------------------------------------------

    def versions_for_entity(self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:
        with self.lock:
            return list(
                self.connection.execute(
                    """
                    SELECT attribute, version, operation, value, valid_from, valid_end,
                           declared_end, recorded_at
                      FROM versions
                     WHERE type = ? AND id = ?
                     ORDER BY attribute, valid_from, version
                    """,
                    (entity_type, entity_id),
                ).fetchall()
            )

    def versions_for_attribute(
        self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str, attribute: str
    ) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:
        with self.lock:
            return list(
                self.connection.execute(
                    """
                    SELECT attribute, version, operation, value, valid_from, valid_end,
                           declared_end, recorded_at
                      FROM versions
                     WHERE type = ? AND id = ? AND attribute = ?
                     ORDER BY valid_from, version
                    """,
                    (entity_type, entity_id, attribute),
                ).fetchall()
            )

    def next_version(self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str, attribute: str) -> int:
        with self.lock:
            row = self.connection.execute(
                """
                SELECT COALESCE(MAX(version), 0) + 1 AS next
                  FROM versions
                 WHERE type = ? AND id = ? AND attribute = ?
                """,
                (entity_type, entity_id, attribute),
            ).fetchone()
        return int(row["next"])

    # -- truncations --------------------------------------------------------

    def truncations_for_entity(self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:
        with self.lock:
            return list(
                self.connection.execute(
                    """
                    SELECT attribute, version, valid_end, recorded_at
                      FROM truncations
                     WHERE type = ? AND id = ?
                     ORDER BY recorded_at, attribute, version
                    """,
                    (entity_type, entity_id),
                ).fetchall()
            )

    def truncate_attribute(
        self,
        entity_type: str,
        entity_id: str,
        attribute: str,
        at: int,
        effective: int,
        recorded_at: int,
    ) -> list[TruncationRecord]:
        """Apply a correction landing at ``at`` that takes effect at ``effective``.

        The version straddling ``at`` keeps its value and only has its
        ``valid_end`` pulled back to ``at``; ``declared_end`` keeps the bound the
        assertion itself declared, so a reader before this write can still see
        the window as it stood when the row was written.

        Every version that starts at or after ``at`` is superseded: it holds no
        valid time from ``at`` onwards.  Its own declared ``valid_end`` stays
        where it was, because a bounded assertion keeps its own bound; the
        truncation records the instant the new value took the window over.

        ``effective`` differs from ``at`` only for a backdated correction with an
        explicit ``valid_from``: the correction is placed in the past but takes
        effect at the instant the version it supersedes did, which is what lets a
        restated past win from ``valid_from`` onwards while the value it
        displaced collapses.

        Every window that this correction closes gets a row in ``truncations``,
        stamped with ``recorded_at`` — the transaction instant the bound was
        learned at, never a business instant.  A truncation is knowledge, so it
        must be datable on the axis a reader filters on: a reader whose
        ``known_at`` is earlier than this write must not see the end it pulled
        back.  Recording one row per event, rather than one stamp per version, is
        what keeps that exact when a later correction pulls the same window back
        twice.

        Only versions recorded no later than this request are touched, so the
        versions inserted by the correction that calls this method cannot
        supersede one another, while a previous correction recorded at the same
        millisecond is still superseded correctly.
        """
        rows = self.connection.execute(
            """
            SELECT version, valid_from, valid_end, declared_end
              FROM versions
             WHERE type = ? AND id = ? AND attribute = ? AND recorded_at <= ?
            """,
            (entity_type, entity_id, attribute, recorded_at),
        ).fetchall()
        events: list[TruncationRecord] = []
        for row in rows:
            version = int(row["version"])
            if int(row["valid_from"]) >= at:
                # A version starting at or after the landing point holds no valid
                # time from there on: it is superseded, not trimmed.
                events.append(
                    (entity_type, entity_id, attribute, version, recorded_at, effective)
                )
                continue
            end = None if row["valid_end"] is None else int(row["valid_end"])
            if end is not None and end <= at:
                # A bound the version declared itself already stops before the
                # landing point, so the correction takes no valid time from it.
                continue
            declared = None if row["declared_end"] is None else int(row["declared_end"])
            self.connection.execute(
                """
                UPDATE versions
                   SET valid_end = ?, declared_end = ?
                 WHERE type = ? AND id = ? AND attribute = ? AND version = ?
                """,
                (
                    at,
                    declared,
                    entity_type,
                    entity_id,
                    attribute,
                    version,
                ),
            )
            events.append(
                (entity_type, entity_id, attribute, version, recorded_at, at)
            )
        if events:
            # Insert one row at a time so the stable rowid of each truncation is
            # known: a version can be superseded more than once inside one
            # batch, which yields truncation rows identical on every column, and
            # only their persistent rowids tell those distinct events apart.
            audit_rows: list[tuple[Any, ...]] = []
            for event in events:
                cursor = self.connection.execute(
                    """
                    INSERT INTO truncations(type, id, attribute, version, recorded_at, valid_end)
                    VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
                    """,
                    event,
                )
                audit_rows.append(
                    (
                        self.audit_event_id(
                            ACTION_WINDOW_TRUNCATED,
                            event[0], event[1], event[2], event[3], event[4], event[5],
                            cursor.lastrowid,
                        ),
                        event[4],
                        ACTION_WINDOW_TRUNCATED,
                        event[0], event[1], event[2], event[3], event[5],
                    )
                )
            self.connection.executemany(
                """
                INSERT INTO audit_events(
                    event_id, recorded_at, action, type, id, attribute, version,
                    operation, value, valid_from, declared_end, valid_end)
                VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, ?)
                """,
                audit_rows,
            )
        return events

    def insert_version(
        self,
        entity_type: str,
        entity_id: str,
        attribute: str,
        version: int,
        operation: str,
        value: Any,
        valid_from: int,
        valid_end: int | None,
        recorded_at: int,
    ) -> None:
        encoded = None if value is None else self.encode(value)
        self.connection.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO versions(type, id, attribute, version, operation, value,
                                 valid_from, valid_end, declared_end, recorded_at)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
            """,
            (
                entity_type,
                entity_id,
                attribute,
                version,
                operation,
                encoded,
                valid_from,
                valid_end,
                valid_end,
                recorded_at,
            ),
        )
        event_id = self.audit_event_id(
            ACTION_VERSION_APPENDED,
            entity_type, entity_id, attribute, version, recorded_at,
            operation, encoded, valid_from, valid_end,
        )
        self.connection.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO audit_events(
                event_id, recorded_at, action, type, id, attribute, version,
                operation, value, valid_from, declared_end, valid_end)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, NULL)
            """,
            (
                event_id,
                recorded_at,
                ACTION_VERSION_APPENDED,
                entity_type,
                entity_id,
                attribute,
                version,
                operation,
                encoded,
                valid_from,
                valid_end,
            ),
        )

    # -- idempotency --------------------------------------------------------

    def idempotent_response(self, key: str, operation: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        row = self.connection.execute(
            "SELECT operation, response FROM idempotency WHERE key = ?", (key,)
        ).fetchone()
        if row is None or row["operation"] != operation:
            return None
        return self.decode(row["response"])

    def remembered_operation(self, key: str) -> str | None:
        row = self.connection.execute(
            "SELECT operation FROM idempotency WHERE key = ?", (key,)
        ).fetchone()
        return None if row is None else str(row["operation"])

    def remember(self, key: str, operation: str, response: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        self.connection.execute(
            "INSERT INTO idempotency(key, operation, response) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
            (key, operation, self.encode(response)),
        )

    # -- audit --------------------------------------------------------------

    def max_audit_seq(self) -> int:
        """The sequence assigned so far; the upper bound a first page pins."""
        with self.lock:
            row = self.connection.execute("SELECT COALESCE(MAX(seq), 0) AS m FROM audit_events").fetchone()
        return int(row["m"])

    def audit_key_exists(self, recorded_at: int, event_id: str, upper_seq: int) -> bool:
        """Whether a cursor's last-returned item is a real row in this store.

        The ledger is append-only, so a cursor this store issued always finds
        its position here.  A token minted against another database (or one
        pointing past the pinned result set) does not, which is how such a
        cursor is reported as unknown instead of silently walking foreign
        data.
        """
        with self.lock:
            row = self.connection.execute(
                "SELECT 1 FROM audit_events WHERE recorded_at = ? AND event_id = ? AND seq <= ?",
                (recorded_at, event_id, upper_seq),
            ).fetchone()
        return row is not None

    def audit_page(
        self,
        *,
        after_recorded_at: int | None,
        after_event_id: str | None,
        upper_seq: int,
        limit: int,
        action: str | None = None,
        entity_type: str | None = None,
        entity_id: str | None = None,
        attribute: str | None = None,
        recorded_from: int | None = None,
        recorded_to: int | None = None,
    ) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:
        """One stable page of audit items.

        Ordering is ``(recorded_at, event_id)`` ascending: ``recorded_at``
        puts the items on the transaction axis, and the event id breaks ties
        inside one millisecond.  Event ids derive from the immutable
        coordinates of the committed event, so that tie-break is stable, never
        reused, and identical after a restart — the order lives in the rows,
        not in a clock reading.

        Pagination is keyset-based: the cursor carries the last seen
        ``(recorded_at, event_id)`` pair, which is what makes pages overlap-
        and gap-free even when several events share a millisecond.
        ``upper_seq`` independently pins the result set: items committed
        after the first page was opened (their ``seq`` is higher) never
        enter later pages, so a concurrent writer cannot move the window
        the cursor walks.
        """
        clauses = ["seq <= ?"]
        parameters: list[Any] = [upper_seq]
        if after_recorded_at is None:
            # Nothing has been consumed yet: the lower recorded-time bound, if
            # any, is the only starting line.
            if recorded_from is not None:
                clauses.append("recorded_at >= ?")
                parameters.append(recorded_from)
        else:
            # Strictly after the last returned key, on the same ordered pair.
            clauses.append("(recorded_at > ? OR (recorded_at = ? AND event_id > ?))")
            parameters.extend([after_recorded_at, after_recorded_at, after_event_id])
            if recorded_from is not None:
                clauses.append("recorded_at >= ?")
                parameters.append(recorded_from)
        if action is not None:
            clauses.append("action = ?")
            parameters.append(action)
        if entity_type is not None:
            clauses.append("type = ?")
            parameters.append(entity_type)
        if entity_id is not None:
            clauses.append("id = ?")
            parameters.append(entity_id)
        if attribute is not None:
            clauses.append("attribute = ?")
            parameters.append(attribute)
        if recorded_to is not None:
            clauses.append("recorded_at < ?")
            parameters.append(recorded_to)
        sql = (
            "SELECT seq, event_id, recorded_at, action, type, id, attribute, version, "
            "operation, value, valid_from, declared_end, valid_end FROM audit_events"
            " WHERE "
            + " AND ".join(clauses)
            + " ORDER BY recorded_at, event_id LIMIT ?"
        )
        parameters.append(limit + 1)
        with self.lock:
            return list(self.connection.execute(sql, parameters).fetchall())

109	def _encode_cursor(filters: AuditFilters, upper_seq: int, after: tuple[int, str] | None) -> str:
110	    payload = json.dumps(
111	        {
112	            "v": _CURSOR_VERSION,
113	            "f": filters.as_cursor(),
114	            "u": upper_seq,
115	            "a": None if after is None else [after[0], after[1]],
116	        },
117	        separators=(",", ":"),
118	        sort_keys=True,
119	    ).encode("utf-8")
120	    signature = hashlib.sha256(_CURSOR_SALT + b"." + payload).digest()
121	    return _b64url(payload) + "." + _b64url(signature)

124	def _decode_cursor(token: str) -> tuple[AuditFilters, int, tuple[int, str] | None]:
125	    bad = ValidationError("cursor is unknown or malformed")
126	    if not isinstance(token, str) or "." not in token:
127	        raise bad
128	    payload_text, signature_text = token.rsplit(".", 1)
129	    try:
130	        payload = _b64url_decode(payload_text)
131	        signature = _b64url_decode(signature_text)
132	    except ValidationError:
133	        raise bad from None
134	    if hashlib.sha256(_CURSOR_SALT + b"." + payload).digest() != signature:
135	        raise bad
136	    try:
137	        state = json.loads(payload)
138	    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError):
139	        raise bad from None
140	    if not isinstance(state, dict) or state.get("v") != _CURSOR_VERSION:
141	        raise bad
142	    upper_seq = state.get("u")
143	    if not isinstance(upper_seq, int) or isinstance(upper_seq, bool) or upper_seq < 0:
144	        raise bad
145	    after_raw = state.get("a")
146	    after: tuple[int, str] | None
147	    if after_raw is None:
148	        after = None
149	    elif (
150	        isinstance(after_raw, list)
151	        and len(after_raw) == 2
152	        and isinstance(after_raw[0], int)
153	        and not isinstance(after_raw[0], bool)
154	        and isinstance(after_raw[1], str)
155	    ):
156	        after = (after_raw[0], after_raw[1])
157	    else:
158	        raise bad
159	    return AuditFilters.from_cursor(state.get("f")), upper_seq, after

225	    def superseded_at(self) -> int | None:
226	        """The transaction instant this version stopped being current, if it has.
227	
228	        That is the instant of a trim, never a business instant, so together with
229	        ``recorded_at`` it bounds a half-open transaction interval and can never
230	        precede it.  When several corrections closed the same window the last one
231	        is the authoritative closure, because it is the one the ledger's final
232	        ``valid_end`` comes from; the earlier trims stay in the row's truncation
233	        events, which is how a reader before a later trim still sees the end that
234	        trim had not yet moved.

238	    def end_known_at(self, known_at: int) -> int | None:

240	
241	        The window end is never later than the bound the assertion declared, so
242	        the answer is the earliest of that declared bound and every trim the
243	        reader already knows about.  A trim recorded after ``known_at`` is not
244	        knowledge yet, so the window it closed is still open ended — that is what
245	        keeps the upper axis exact.
246	        """
247	        end = self.declared_end
248	        for event in self.known_truncations(known_at):
249	            end = event.valid_end if end is None else min(end, event.valid_end)
250	        if end is None:
251	            return None
252	        # ``valid_end`` already folds in every trim, including ones this reader
253	        # has not learned yet, so it is only ever a safe ceiling for the end the
254	        # reader knows — never a later bound leaking backwards.
255	        return self.valid_end if self.valid_end is None else min(end, self.valid_end)

290	def known_windows(versions: list[Version], known_at: int) -> list[Token]:
291	    """Reconstruct the valid windows of one attribute as known at ``known_at``.
292	
293	    Every version is known from its ``recorded_at`` onwards, and every truncation
294	    it carries from the ``recorded_at`` of that truncation onwards.  Working from
295	    the newest version the reader can see back to the oldest, a version holds
296	    valid time from its own ``valid_from`` until the earliest of:
297	
298	    * ``valid_from`` of the next version the reader can see, because the value
299	      written later is the one in force from then on;
300	    * the end it carries for that reader, which is its declared ``valid_end`` or,
301	      while the trim that pulled the end back is still unknown, nothing at all;
302	    * the instant a correction already known at ``known_at`` starts writing
303	      there, which is where the chain of visible corrections takes over.
304	
305	    A version whose only displacers are recorded after ``known_at`` keeps an open
306	    ended window, because at that instant nobody had written the bound — that
307	    rule is what keeps a transaction-time view exact.  Tokens come back in
308	    transaction order, oldest first.  Retraction rows always carry an empty
309	    window: they exist to mark the instant an attribute ceased to exist.
310	    """
311	    ordered = sorted(versions, key=lambda item: (item.valid_from, item.version))
312	    tokens: list[Token] = []
313	    takeover: int | None = None
314	    for index in range(len(ordered) - 1, -1, -1):
315	        version = ordered[index]
316	        if version.recorded_at > known_at:
317	            # Not recorded yet for this reader, and it could not have displaced
318	            # anything either: it is invisible to the whole pass.
319	            continue
320	        following = next(
321	            (
322	                ordered[other]
323	                for other in range(index + 1, len(ordered))
324	                if ordered[other].recorded_at <= known_at
325	            ),
326	            None,
327	        )
328	        if version.operation == "retract":
329	            # A retraction never holds valid time of its own; it only closes the
330	            # window in front of it.
331	            end: int | None = version.valid_from
332	        else:
333	            end = version.end_known_at(known_at)
334	            if following is not None:
335	                # A version the reader can see takes over where it begins.
336	                end = following.valid_from if end is None else min(end, following.valid_from)
337	            if takeover is not None:
338	                # A correction already known at ``known_at`` starts writing at
339	                # that instant, which is the end of everything before it.
340	                end = takeover if end is None else min(end, takeover)
341	        tokens.append((version, version.valid_from, end))
342	        takeover = version.valid_from
343	    tokens.sort(key=lambda token: (token[0].recorded_at, token[0].version))
344	    return tokens

347	def complete_windows(versions: list[Version], known_at: int) -> list[Token]:
348	    """The windows as they stand in the ledger, for a history listing.
349	
350	    Every version the reader can see keeps the end the ledger records for it,
351	    with any trim the reader cannot know about yet left out, so this is the
352	    full-knowledge view of the ledger for that transaction instant rather than a
353	    projection: a window a correction pulled back shows the pulled back end once
354	    that correction is knowable, and a value displaced by a backdated
355	    restatement keeps the part of its own window that no later version took over.
356	    """
357	    ordered = sorted(versions, key=lambda item: (item.valid_from, item.version))
358	    tokens: list[Token] = []
359	    for index, version in enumerate(ordered):
360	        if version.recorded_at > known_at:
361	            # Recorded after the reader's instant, so this reader never saw it.
362	            continue
363	        end = version.end_known_at(known_at)
364	        successor = next(
365	            (
366	                ordered[other]
367	                for other in range(index + 1, len(ordered))
368	                if ordered[other].recorded_at <= known_at
369	            ),
370	            None,
371	        )
372	        if successor is not None:
373	            end = successor.valid_from if end is None else min(end, successor.valid_from)
374	        tokens.append((version, version.valid_from, end))
375	    tokens.sort(key=lambda token: (token[0].valid_from, token[0].version))
376	    return tokens

379	def project(tokens: list[Token], at: int) -> Token | None:
380	    """Select the value that was in force at business instant ``at``.
381	
382	    Tokens arrive in transaction order, newest first.  A backdated correction can
383	    leave two windows that touch: the value it displaced keeps the window it had,
384	    and the restated value covers the earlier part of it.  The value written last
385	    is the one the ledger believes from the instant it took effect, so the
386	    newest match wins.
387	    """
388	    for token in reversed(tokens):
389	        start, end = token[1], token[2]
390	        if start <= at and (end is None or at < end):
391	            return token
392	    return None

395	def _projection_content_same(first: Projection, second: Projection) -> bool:
396	    """Whether two projections carry the same public data content.
397	
398	    What counts is what a read reports as data: every attribute's value and
399	    the valid window it holds.  The version number that supplies the value
400	    and the transaction instant the row was recorded at are storage
401	    bookkeeping, so they may differ freely without making the records differ.
402	    """
403	    if set(first) != set(second):
404	        return False
405	    for name in first:
406	        left, right = first[name], second[name]
407	        if not value_same(left[0], right[0]):
408	            return False
409	        if (left[2], left[3], left[4]) != (right[2], right[3], right[4]):
410	            return False
411	    return True

441	    """Bitemporal entity store: valid time on one axis, transaction time on the other."""

453	            if valid_from > moment:

456	            valid_from = moment

459	            return self._create_core(

467	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:

469	        correction = Correction.parse(raw, now)

472	            return self._correct_core(entity_type, entity_id, correction, recorded_at)

476	    def run_batch(self, raw: Any, key: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
477	        """Atomically apply an ordered list of creates and corrections.
478	
479	        Every item shares one transaction instant, so the whole batch is one
480	        point on the transaction axis: later items see earlier items' effects,
481	        but no outside reader ever sees a partially applied batch.  Any invalid
482	        or conflicting item aborts the transaction and nothing is stored.
483	        """
484	        moment = self.store.now()
485	        operations = parse_batch(raw, moment)
486	        # Entities this very batch will create, so a correction whose creation
487	        # sits later in the array can be told apart from one that names an
488	        # entity nobody will ever create: the first is an ordering conflict,
489	        # the second is simply not found.
490	        created_here = {
491	            (item.entity_type, item.entity_id)
492	            for item in operations
493	            if isinstance(item, BatchCreate)
494	        }
495	
496	        def action(recorded_at: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
497	            results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
498	            seen_creates: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
499	            for index, item in enumerate(operations, start=1):
500	                target = (item.entity_type, item.entity_id)
501	                try:
502	                    if isinstance(item, BatchCreate):
503	                        start = item.valid_from if item.valid_from is not None else recorded_at
504	                        document = self._create_core(
505	                            item.entity_type,
506	                            item.entity_id,
507	                            item.attributes,
508	                            start,
509	                            recorded_at,
510	                        )
511	                        seen_creates.add(target)
512	                        document["operation"] = "create"
513	                    elif isinstance(item, BatchCorrect):
514	                        try:
515	                            document = self._correct_core(
516	                                item.entity_type,
517	                                item.entity_id,
518	                                item.correction,
519	                                recorded_at,
520	                            )
521	                        except NotFoundError:
522	                            if target in created_here and target not in seen_creates:
523	                                raise ConflictError(
524	                                    f"entity {item.entity_type}/{item.entity_id} is "
525	                                    "corrected before it is created"
526	                                )
527	                            raise
528	                        document["operation"] = "correct"
529	                    else:  # pragma: no cover - parse_batch only yields the two kinds
530	                        raise ValidationError("unknown batch operation")
531	                except TimeVaultError as error:
532	                    message = str(error)
533	                    if not message.startswith("operation "):
534	                        raise type(error)(f"operation {index}: {message}") from error
535	                    raise
536	                results.append(document)
537	            return {"recorded_at": iso(recorded_at), "results": results}
538	
539	        return self._idempotent(key, _batch_operation_name(raw), action, moment)

594	    def diff(
595	        self,
596	        entity_type: str,
597	        entity_id: str,
598	        start: Any,
599	        end: Any,
600	        known_at: Any = None,
601	        names: list[str] | None = None,
602	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
603	        start = instant(start, "from")
604	        end = instant(end, "to")
605	        known_at = self.store.now() if known_at is None else instant(known_at, "known_at")
606	        if end <= start:
607	            raise ValidationError("to must be strictly later than from")
608	        if names is not None and len(set(names)) != len(names):
609	            raise ValidationError("attribute may not be repeated")
610	        left = self._projection(entity_type, entity_id, start, known_at)
611	        right = self._projection(entity_type, entity_id, end, known_at)
612	        selected = sorted(set(left) | set(right))
613	        if names is not None:
614	            wanted = set(names)
615	            unknown = sorted(wanted - set(self._all_attributes(entity_type, entity_id)))
616	            if unknown:
617	                raise ValidationError(f"unknown attribute(s): {', '.join(unknown)}")
618	            selected = [name for name in selected if name in wanted]
619	
620	        changes = []
621	        for name in selected:
622	            before = left.get(name)
623	            after = right.get(name)
624	            if before is None and after is None:

1	# TimeVault
2	
3	TimeVault is a small bitemporal entity store. Every attribute value it holds is
4	stamped on two independent time axes:
5	
6	- **valid time** — when the fact was true in the business world
7	  (`valid_from` inclusive, `valid_end` exclusive);
8	- **transaction time** — when the system came to know the fact (`recorded_at`).
9	
10	A correction never overwrites history. It appends a new version, truncates the
11	valid window of the value it supersedes, and leaves that earlier value readable
12	in the history forever. Reads take one instant on each axis (`as_of` and
13	`known_at`), which is what makes "what did we believe on Tuesday about last
14	March?" answerable.
15	
16	## Requirements
17	
18	- Python 3.11 or newer
19	- no third-party runtime dependencies
20	
21	## Run the service
22	
23	```bash
24	PYTHONPATH=src python -m timevault.server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 --database timevault.db
25	```
26	
27	The process prints `TimeVault listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080` after it has
28	bound the port.
29	
30	## The two axes
31	
32	| axis | written by | read by | interval |
33	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
34	| valid time | `valid_from` / `valid_end` of a fact | `as_of` | `[from, end)` |
35	| transaction time | the injected clock, one instant per write | `known_at` | `[recorded_at, superseded_at)` here, `[recorded_at, now)` if still current |
36	
37	Both coordinates of the transaction interval are transaction instants: `recorded_at`
38	is when the write was recorded and `superseded_at` is when a later write stopped
39	the version being current. Neither is ever a business instant, so the interval can
40	never run backwards. `superseded_at` is `null` while the version is still current.
41	
42	Both axes accept an RFC 3339 instant such as `2024-05-31T00:00:00Z`, an integer
43	count of milliseconds since the Unix epoch, or a float count of seconds since
44	the epoch. Internally every coordinate is an integer millisecond count, so
45	ordering and equality are exact. A `GET` with no query projects at the current
46	instant on both axes.
47	
48	`known_at` is a cutoff: a version recorded after it does not exist for that read,
49	so a window that a later correction truncated still looks open ended at that
50	earlier transaction time.
51	
52	## Data model
53	
54	An entity is a set of named attributes under a `type` and an `id`. Values must
55	be a string, a number, a boolean, or `null`; objects and arrays are rejected.
56	The ledger keeps one row per **attribute version**:
57	
58	| field | axis | meaning |
59	| --- | --- | --- |
60	| `version` | — | per-attribute counter, from 1, never reused |
61	| `operation` | — | `assert` (holds `value`) or `retract` (holds nothing) |
62	| `value` | — | the asserted value, `null` for a retraction |
63	| `valid_from` | valid | inclusive start of the valid window |
64	| `declared_end` | valid | the exclusive end the assertion declared, `null` if it declared none; never moves |
65	| `valid_end` | valid | exclusive end of the window once every correction so far has applied its trim, `null` while open ended |
66	| `recorded_at` | transaction | when the write request was recorded |
67	| `superseded_at` | transaction | when a later write stopped this version being current, `null` while current |
68	
69	`declared_end` and `valid_end` differ exactly when a correction pulled the window
70	back: the declared bound is what the row was written with, the effective bound is
71	where the last trim of that window left it. The two together are what let a
72	reader before the trim see the open ended window the row actually had. A single
73	window can be trimmed more than once, by a correction in force and then by a
74	backdated restatement that lands earlier still; each trim appends its own
75	`truncations` row, so a reader between two trims sees the end the first one left
76	and never the earlier end the second one pulled it back to.
77	
78	Rows are append-only. A correction appends its own row, and the only columns it
79	ever updates on an older row are `valid_end` and `declared_end` — that update is
80	the trim. Every trim is also appended to the `truncations` table, one row per
81	event, stamped with the trim's **transaction instant**:
82	`(type, id, attribute, version, recorded_at, valid_end)`. A trim is knowledge, so
83	the truncation carries the instant it was learned; a per-version stamp instead of
84	one row per event could not describe a window trimmed twice, because the second
85	trim would overwrite the first one's instant.
86	
87	### How a write lands
88	
89	`PUT /entities/{type}/{id}` takes `as_of` (the correction's effective instant,
90	default *now*) and a non-empty `facts` array. A fact is
91	`{attribute, value, valid_from?, valid_end?, deleted?}` and is placed at its own
92	`valid_from`, which defaults to the correction's `as_of`. For the attribute a
93	fact touches:
94	
95	1. every version whose `valid_from` is at or after the landing point is
96	   superseded — it keeps its value and its own `valid_end` bound, but no `as_of`
97	   selects it, because a newer version took over where it began; the trim is
98	   recorded with the transaction instant of this write;
99	2. the version straddling the landing point keeps its value and only has its
100	   `valid_end` pulled back to the landing point, so the new value replaces it
101	   from then on;
102	3. the fact is appended: an `assert` holding the given value and an optional
103	   declared `valid_end`, or a `retract` with an empty window at the landing
104	   point when `deleted` is `true`.
105	
106	A fact at or after the correction's effective instant takes effect immediately,
107	so the value it displaced stops there. A fact that declares its own earlier
108	`valid_from` is a **backdated restatement**: it is placed at that instant and
109	takes over the valid time from there, which cuts the window of the value it
110	displaced and usually leaves that value holding only the part of its own window
111	that nothing newer claimed. A restatement never rewrites the interval between its
112	own instant and the correction's, and the flat result is always a set of
113	non-overlapping windows: each version holds valid time from its `valid_from`
114	until the next version (in valid time) begins, its own declared `valid_end`, or
115	the `valid_end` its trims left it, whichever comes first.
116	
117	A retraction is a row with an empty valid window at the instant the attribute
118	ceased to exist. It is never selectable by `as_of`; it exists so the window
119	before it has a boundary and so the history records that the attribute was
120	withdrawn rather than corrected. The value it withdrew keeps its own
121	`valid_end`, so that window still looks open ended for a `known_at` earlier than
122	the retraction was recorded.
123	
124	### How a read projects
125	
126	For one attribute and a reader's `known_at`:
127	
128	1. discard every version recorded after `known_at`, and every trim recorded
129	   after it — the reader could not see either;
130	2. a remaining version holds valid time from its `valid_from` until the earliest
131	   of: the `valid_from` of the next version the reader can see, its declared
132	   `valid_end`, and the instant a trim the reader can see pulled its window back;
133	3. a version whose only truncation was written after `known_at` keeps an open
134	   ended window for that reader, because at that instant nobody had written the
135	   bound. No stored `valid_end` leaks backwards past the write that put it there;
136	4. a retraction row always holds an empty window, and it closes the window in
137	   front of it only from the instant it was recorded onwards;
138	5. `as_of` selects the newest version whose half-open window contains it. If no
139	   attribute is in effect, that attribute is absent from the response, and an
140	   entity with nothing in effect at that instant is `not_found`.
141	
142	Step 3 is what makes the upper axis exact.
143	
144	#### Worked example for step 3
145	
146	Three instants, one entity, one correction:
147	
148	| event | transaction instant | what it writes |
149	| --- | --- | --- |
150	| W1 | `2026-10-02T06:30:16.984Z` | `tier = gold`, valid from `2024-01-01`, open ended |
151	| W2 | `2026-10-02T06:30:16.987Z` | `tier = platinum`, effective `2024-03-01`; trims gold to end at `2024-03-01` |
152	
153	Reading `GET /entities/account/acct-1?as_of=2024-04-01T00:00:00Z` at three
154	`known_at` values, the answer follows by hand from rule 2 and rule 3:
155	
156	| `known_at` | versions visible | trims visible | gold's window | window at `2024-04-01` contains it? | answer |
157	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
158	| `06:30:16.985Z` | gold | none | `[2024-01-01, ∞)` | yes | `gold` |
159	| `06:30:16.986Z` | gold | none | `[2024-01-01, ∞)` | yes | `gold` |
160	| `06:30:16.987Z` | gold, platinum | gold ends `2024-03-01` | `[2024-01-01, 2024-03-01)` | no | `platinum` |
161	
162	The first two rows are rule 3: W2's trim is recorded at `.987Z`, so at `.985Z`
163	and `.986Z` the trim does not exist yet and gold still runs to `[2024-01-01, ∞)`.
164	In the last row the reader is at W2's own instant, so it sees both the trim that
165	ends gold at `2024-03-01` and the platinum version that takes over there;
166	`2024-04-01` falls in platinum's window, which contains it.
167	
168	## HTTP API
169	
170	All bodies are JSON. Unknown body fields and unknown query parameters are
171	rejected with `validation_error`. Every state-changing POST and PUT requires an
172	`Idempotency-Key` header; replaying a key returns the first response and writes
173	nothing new.
174	
175	### Health
176	
177	```http
178	GET /health
179	```
180	
181	```json
182	{"status":"ok"}
183	```
184	
185	### Create an entity
186	
187	```http
188	POST /entities/account
189	Idempotency-Key: create-1
190	
191	{
192	  "id": "acct-1",
193	  "attributes": {"status": "active", "tier": "gold"},
194	  "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"
195	}
196	```
197	
198	Returns HTTP 201. `valid_from` defaults to the current instant and must not be in
199	the future. Every attribute starts at version 1 with an open ended window. The
200	response is the projection at the current instant plus `created_at` — the same
201	shape as a read, and a projection carries only the fields a read reports:
202	
203	```json
204	{"type": "account", "id": "acct-1",
205	 "as_of": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z", "known_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z",
206	 "created_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z",
207	 "attributes": {
208	   "status": {"value": "active", "version": 1, "operation": "assert",
209	              "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z", "valid_end": null,
210	              "declared_end": null,
211	              "recorded_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z"},
212	   "tier": {"value": "gold", "version": 1, "operation": "assert",
213	            "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z", "valid_end": null,
214	            "declared_end": null,
215	            "recorded_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z"}}}
216	```
217	
218	Creating the same `type`/`id` again is `conflict` (409).
219	
220	### Correct an entity
221	
222	```http
223	PUT /entities/account/acct-1
224	Idempotency-Key: fix-1
225	
226	{
227	  "as_of": "2024-03-01T00:00:00Z",
228	  "facts": [
229	    {"attribute": "tier", "value": "platinum"},
230	    {"attribute": "region", "value": "emea"},
231	    {"attribute": "status", "deleted": true}
232	  ]
233	}
234	```
235	
236	Returns HTTP 200 with the projection at the current instant, so the response
237	always shows the entity as it is now believed to be; a write is never a 404, even
238	if the correction leaves nothing in effect right now. Afterwards `tier` holds
239	`platinum` and `region` exists from 2024-03-01, `status` holds nothing from
240	2024-03-01, and the earlier `tier` and `status` values remain readable through
241	`as_of` before 2024-03-01 and through `/history`.
242	
243	A fact that would create an empty window (for example a `valid_end` at or before
244	the window start) is a `validation_error`, because a version's window is never
245	made empty by an ordinary correction.
246	
247	### Batch import
248	
249	```http
250	POST /batch
251	Idempotency-Key: import-1
252	
253	{
254	  "operations": [
255	    {"operation": "create", "type": "account", "id": "acct-1",
256	     "attributes": {"status": "active", "tier": "gold"},
257	     "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
258	    {"operation": "correct", "type": "account", "id": "acct-1",
259	     "as_of": "2024-03-01T00:00:00Z",
260	     "facts": [{"attribute": "tier", "value": "platinum"}]},
261	    {"operation": "correct", "type": "account", "id": "acct-1",
262	     "facts": [{"attribute": "region", "value": "emea"}]}
263	  ]
264	}
265	```
266	
267	Returns HTTP 200. The body must be an object containing only an `operations`
268	array of between 1 and 1000 items, and the request requires an
269	`Idempotency-Key` header. Each item is one of:
270	
271	- `create` — `type`, `id`, `attributes`, and an optional `valid_from`, with the
272	  same field semantics as `POST /entities/{type}`;
273	- `correct` — `type`, `id`, optional `as_of`, and `facts`, with the same field
274	  semantics as `PUT /entities/{type}/{id}`.
275	
276	Operations apply in the order given, so a later item sees the result of the
277	earlier ones: the same request may create an entity and then correct it, and it
278	may append several history segments to an entity that already existed. An item
279	that corrects an entity the same batch creates **later** is a `conflict`;
280	correcting an entity nobody creates is `not_found`; a duplicate create (against
281	an existing entity or an earlier item) is a `conflict`. A batch item that fails
282	any check reports the one-based index of the item, for example
283	`operation 2: as_of must not be in the future`. Structural and field problems
284	are `validation_error`.
285	
286	The whole batch is one write: it commits at a single transaction instant under
287	one transaction, so every version and trim it produces carries the same
288	`recorded_at`, and any failing item aborts the entire request — nothing is
289	stored and no version numbers are consumed. Different batches submitted
290	concurrently commit one after another, so version numbers stay continuous and
291	valid windows never overlap; a reader never sees a partially applied batch.
292	
293	```json
294	{"recorded_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z",
295	 "results": [
296	   {"operation": "create", "type": "account", "id": "acct-1",
297	    "as_of": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z", "known_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z",
298	    "created_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z",
299	    "attributes": {"tier": {"value": "gold", "version": 1, "operation": "assert",
300	                            "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
301	                            "valid_end": null,
302	                            "recorded_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z"}}},
303	   {"operation": "correct", "type": "account", "id": "acct-1",
304	    "as_of": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z", "known_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z",
305	    "attributes": {"tier": {"value": "platinum", "version": 2, "operation": "assert",
306	                            "valid_from": "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z",
307	                            "valid_end": null,
308	                            "recorded_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z"}}}]}
309	```
310	
311	`results` is the same length and order as `operations`. Each result has the
312	shape the matching single-entity write would return (a `create` result carries
313	`created_at`, a `correct` result does not), plus an `operation` field naming its
314	type. The top-level `recorded_at` is the batch's transaction instant in the
315	same instant format the rest of the API uses. After the batch returns, the
316	ordinary `GET`, `/history`, and `/diff` entry points read the resulting state
317	exactly as if each operation had been written individually at that instant.
318	
319	Replaying a key returns the first batch's stored 200 response and writes
320	nothing, so replayed batches add no versions; reusing a key for a different
321	batch request is a `conflict`.
322	
323	### Read an entity
324	
325	```http
326	GET /entities/account/acct-1?as_of=2024-02-01T00:00:00Z
327	GET /entities/account/acct-1?as_of=2024-02-01T00:00:00Z&known_at=2024-05-15T00:00:00Z
328	GET /entities/account/acct-1
329	```
330	
331	```json
332	{"type": "account", "id": "acct-1",
333	 "as_of": "2024-02-01T00:00:00.000Z", "known_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z",
334	 "attributes": {
335	   "status": {"value": "active", "version": 1, "operation": "assert",
336	              "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
337	              "valid_end": "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z",
338	              "recorded_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z"},
339	   "tier": {"value": "gold", "version": 1, "operation": "assert",
340	            "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
341	            "valid_end": "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z",
342	            "recorded_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z"}}}
343	```
344	
345	Both parameters default to the current instant. `valid_end` in a response is the
346	window as it appears to that reader, so it reflects the trims recorded up to
347	`known_at` and nothing later. An instant before the entity's first valid
348	time, one where no attribute is in effect, or a `known_at` earlier than the
349	entity was recorded, is `not_found`.
350	
351	### Read the history
352	
353	```http
354	GET /entities/account/acct-1/history
355	GET /entities/account/acct-1/history?known_at=2024-05-15T00:00:00Z
356	```
357	
358	Every version of every attribute, ordered by valid time, with the window as it
359	stands in the ledger for that reader:
360	
361	```json
362	{"type": "account", "id": "acct-1",
363	 "created_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z", "known_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z",
364	 "attributes": [{"attribute": "tier", "versions": [
365	   {"attribute": "tier", "version": 1, "operation": "assert", "value": "gold",
366	    "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z", "valid_from_ms": 1704067200000,
367	    "valid_end": "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z", "valid_end_ms": 1709251200000,
368	    "declared_end": null,
369	    "recorded_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z",
370	    "superseded_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z"},
371	   {"attribute": "tier", "version": 2, "operation": "assert", "value": "platinum",
372	    "valid_from": "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z", "valid_from_ms": 1709251200000,
373	    "valid_end": null, "valid_end_ms": null, "declared_end": null,
374	    "recorded_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z", "superseded_at": null}]}]}
375	```
376	
377	`superseded_at` is the transaction instant a later write stopped the version
378	being current, and it is `null` while the version is still current. It is not the
379	business instant the window ended at: that is `valid_end`, and for version 1 the
380	two are different instants, `2024-03-01` against `2024-05-31`. Gold was written
381	on `2024-05-01` (`recorded_at`) and superseded on `2024-05-31` (`superseded_at`),
382	so its transaction interval is `[2024-05-01, 2024-05-31)` — it can never be
383	inverted, whatever the effective instant of the correction was.
384	
385	`declared_end` is the bound the assertion itself declared, `null` here because
386	gold declared none; `valid_end` is where the correction trimmed it. `recorded_at`
387	filters out versions recorded after the reader's instant, and the same cutoff
388	hides the trims recorded after it, so a correction recorded after `known_at`
389	disappears from that earlier history view and the window it trimmed reads as open
390	ended there.
391	
392	### Diff two business instants
393	
394	```http
395	GET /diff?type=account&id=acct-1&from=2024-02-01T00:00:00Z&to=2024-04-01T00:00:00Z
396	GET /diff?type=account&id=acct-1&from=...&to=...&known_at=2024-05-15T00:00:00Z&attribute=tier
397	```
398	
399	Compares the two projections under one knowledge cutoff (the current instant
400	unless `known_at` is given) and reports one entry per attribute whose value
401	differs:
402	
403	```json
404	{"type": "account", "id": "acct-1",
405	 "from": "2024-02-01T00:00:00.000Z", "to": "2024-04-01T00:00:00.000Z",
406	 "known_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z",
407	 "changes": [
408	   {"attribute": "region", "change": "added", "before": null,
409	    "after": {"value": "emea", "version": 1, "operation": "assert",
410	              "valid_from": "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z", "valid_end": null,
411	              "recorded_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z"}},
412	   {"attribute": "status", "change": "removed",
413	    "before": {"value": "active", "version": 1, "operation": "assert",
414	               "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
415	               "valid_end": "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z",
416	               "recorded_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z"},
417	    "after": null}]}
418	```
419	
420	`change` is `added` when the attribute holds nothing at `from` and something at
421	`to`, `removed` for the reverse, and `changed` when both hold a different value.
422	An attribute whose value carried across the interval is not a change, even if a
423	different version supplies it. `attribute` may be repeated to narrow the result;
424	naming an attribute the entity never had is a `validation_error`. `to` must be
425	strictly later than `from`, and the entity must be in effect at both instants.
426	
427	### Diff two snapshot facets
428	
429	```http
430	GET /snapshot-diff?type=account&first_as_of=2024-04-01T00:00:00Z&first_known_at=2024-05-15T00:00:00Z&second_as_of=2024-04-01T00:00:00Z&second_known_at=2024-06-30T00:00:00Z
431	GET /snapshot-diff?type=account&id=acct-1&first_known_at=2024-05-15T00:00:00Z
432	GET /snapshot-diff
433	```
434	
435	Compares the visible records of a scope at two **facets**, where each facet is
436	an independent `(as_of, known_at)` pair evaluated under exactly the visibility
437	rules of a plain read: a correction recorded after a facet's `known_at` — and
438	any trim it carried — does not exist for that facet. Every coordinate defaults
439	to the current instant and accepts the same forms as `as_of`/`known_at` on a
440	read. The scope is optional: `type` and `id` together name one entity, `type`
441	alone names every entity of that type, and no scope at all spans the whole
442	store. Naming `id` without `type` is a `validation_error`.
443	
444	Entities are partitioned into three categories:
445	
446	```json
447	{"first": {"as_of": "2024-04-01T00:00:00.000Z", "known_at": "2024-05-15T00:00:00.000Z"},
448	 "second": {"as_of": "2024-04-01T00:00:00.000Z", "known_at": "2024-06-30T00:00:00.000Z"},
449	 "added": [{"type": "account", "id": "acct-2", "record": {"type": "account", "id": "acct-2",
450	            "as_of": "2024-04-01T00:00:00.000Z", "known_at": "2024-06-30T00:00:00.000Z",
451	            "attributes": {"tier": {"value": "silver", "version": 1, "operation": "assert",
452	                                    "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
453	                                    "valid_end": null,
454	                                    "recorded_at": "2024-06-30T00:00:00.000Z"}}}}],
455	 "removed": [],
456	 "changed": [{"type": "account", "id": "acct-1",
457	              "before": {"type": "account", "id": "acct-1",
458	                         "as_of": "2024-04-01T00:00:00.000Z",
459	                         "known_at": "2024-05-15T00:00:00.000Z",
460	                         "attributes": {"tier": {"value": "gold", "version": 1,
461	                                                 "operation": "assert",
462	                                                 "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
463	                                                 "valid_end": null,
464	                                                 "recorded_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z"}}},
465	              "after": {"type": "account", "id": "acct-1",
466	                        "as_of": "2024-04-01T00:00:00.000Z",
467	                        "known_at": "2024-06-30T00:00:00.000Z",
468	                        "attributes": {"tier": {"value": "platinum", "version": 2,
469	                                                "operation": "assert",
470	                                                "valid_from": "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z",
471	                                                "valid_end": null,
472	                                                "recorded_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z"}}}}]}
473	```
474	
475	`added` holds the entities visible only at the second facet, each with its full
476	record as the second facet sees it; `removed` holds those visible only at the
477	first facet, with the first facet's record; `changed` holds those visible at
478	both whose public data content differs, with both records. An entity whose
479	record is the same at both facets is not part of the result. Content is what a
480	read reports as data — attribute values and their valid windows — so a
481	difference only in the version number that supplies a value or in the
482	transaction instant it was recorded at is not a change. Each category is
483	ordered by the stable `(type, id)` identifier, so repeating the query over the
484	same data always yields the same document. An empty store, a scope with nothing
485	in it, or two identical facets yields three empty categories rather than an
486	error. The query is read-only: it appends no versions and moves no transaction
487	time, and data written through `POST /batch` takes part in the same computation
488	as data written one request at a time.
489	
490	### Trace ledger changes
491	
492	```http
493	GET /audit
494	GET /audit?type=account&id=acct-1&attribute=tier
495	GET /audit?action=version_appended&recorded_from=2024-05-01T00:00:00Z&recorded_to=2024-06-01T00:00:00Z
496	GET /audit?limit=50&cursor=…
497	```
498	
499	Every committed write leaves two kinds of immutable entries on the audit
500	ledger, one per **committed** event:
501	
502	- `version_appended` — one item per version a create or correction appended;
503	- `window_truncated` — one item per window a correction closed (both the
504	  straddling trim and each supersession), carrying the transaction instant the
505	  bound was learned at.
506	
507	A request that fails or rolls back leaves nothing; an idempotent replay writes
508	nothing and therefore adds no item. Every item of one `POST /batch` shares the
509	batch's single `recorded_at`. The query itself is strictly read-only.
510	
511	Items are ordered by `recorded_at` ascending; within one millisecond the
512	`event_id` — a stable, never-reused digest of the item's immutable committed
513	coordinates — determines the order, and that order is identical after a
514	restart. Filters:
515	
516	| parameter | effect |
517	| --- | --- |
518	| `type` | only items for entities of this type |
519	| `id` | only items for this entity; requires `type` |
520	| `attribute` | only items touching this attribute |
521	| `action` | `version_appended` or `window_truncated` |
522	| `recorded_from` | inclusive transaction-time lower bound |
523	| `recorded_to` | exclusive transaction-time upper bound |
524	| `limit` | page size, 1–500, default 100 |
525	| `cursor` | continue a previously pinned result set |
526	
527	The time bounds accept the same forms as every other transaction-time input
528	(RFC 3339 string, epoch milliseconds, or float seconds) and are interpreted as
529	the half-open interval `[recorded_from, recorded_to)`; `recorded_from` must be
530	strictly earlier than `recorded_to`. Unknown parameters, a limit outside
531	1–500, an `id` without a `type`, an unknown or corrupted cursor, and any other
532	malformed argument are `validation_error`. A legal range that matches nothing
533	— an empty store included — is `200` with an empty `items` and a `null`
534	cursor, not an error.
535	
536	```json
537	{"items": [
538	  {"event_id": "2e619c6b…", "recorded_at": "2024-05-01T00:00:00.000Z",
539	   "type": "account", "id": "acct-1", "attribute": "tier", "version": 1,
540	   "action": "version_appended", "operation": "assert", "value": "gold",
541	   "valid_from": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z", "declared_end": null},
542	  {"event_id": "41e623c2…", "recorded_at": "2024-05-31T00:00:00.000Z",
543	   "type": "account", "id": "acct-1", "attribute": "tier", "version": 1,
544	   "action": "window_truncated", "valid_end": "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z"}],
545	 "next_cursor": null}
546	```
547	
548	Every item carries `event_id`, `recorded_at`, `type`, `id`, `attribute`,
549	`version`, and `action`. A `version_appended` item additionally carries the
550	exact `operation`, `value`, `valid_from`, and `declared_end` it committed with
551	— including a retraction's null value and empty window — read off the audit
552	row rather than the version's current state, so a later correction can never
553	rewrite an older item. A `window_truncated` item carries only the `valid_end`
554	learned by that truncation. Together, `type`/`id`/`attribute`/`version` locate
555	the source row behind any ordinary read or `/history` result.
556	
557	The first query returns a cursor when more items match; the cursor pins the
558	result set's upper bound and keeps the filters, so a write that commits
559	concurrently afterwards never enters later pages, and walking the pages
560	neither repeats nor skips an item. When `cursor` is present every other filter
561	is forbidden, though `limit` may change between pages. The cursor is opaque
562	and signed; one issued against another database is unknown and is rejected.
563	
564	Databases created before this entry point existed need no migration: on open,
565	their committed `versions` and `truncations` rows are projected once into the
566	audit ledger (the unique event ids make the projection idempotent), so
567	pre-upgrade history is auditable exactly like new writes.
568	
569	## Errors
570	
571	```json
572	{"error":{"code":"validation_error","message":"human readable detail"}}
573	```
574	
575	Validation errors return 400, unknown routes and entities that are not in effect
576	at the requested instant return 404, and a duplicate entity, a reused
577	idempotency key, or a correction that would predate the entity returns 409.
578	
579	## Invariants
580	
581	- The ledger is append-only; a correction only ever moves a `valid_end` earlier
582	  and never deletes a value.
583	- Valid windows of one attribute never overlap.
584	- The same `(as_of, known_at)` pair always yields the same projection.
585	- `known_at` never exposes a correction recorded after it, and never exposes a
586	  trim recorded after it either.
587	- A transaction interval never runs backwards: `superseded_at` is a transaction
588	  instant at or after `recorded_at`, never a business instant.
589	- A version never has `valid_end` before `valid_from`, and a window that a
590	  correction made empty stays in the history carrying
591	  `valid_end == valid_from`. The empty window of a retraction row is
592	  intentional, not an overlap.
593	
594	## Tests
595	
596	```bash
597	PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
598	```
599
